papers.title: Time-and-band limiting for symmetric classical Dunkl orthogonal polynomials
papers.abstract: The problem of ''time and band limiting'' has been previously considered for expansions in orthonormal polynomials that are common eigenfunctions of some second order differential operator. In this paper we consider the situation of orthonormal polynomials that are eigenfunctions of some second order differential-difference operator as introduced by Ch. Dunkl. These polynomials appear already in the work of G. Szeg\H{o} and at the same time play a role in supersymmetric quantum mechanics.

papers.title: Spectra of Multivariate Vandermonde Matrices and Min-max Error Bounds for the High-dimensional Super-resolution Problem
papers.abstract: We study multivariate rectangular Vandermonde matrices $U_N$ whose rows are indexed by the grid $G_N=\{-N,\ldots,N\}^d, $ and whose columns correspond to irregularly spaced points on the unit $d$-dimensional torus. Motivated by the problem of super-resolution (recovery of spike trains from low frequency noisy measurements), we consider configurations in which the points form several clusters, with points within each cluster separated by at most $h$ and distinct clusters are well-separated. We show that the column subspaces associated with different clusters are nearly orthogonal, i.e. for $N \rightarrow \infty, Nh \ll 1$, the minimal principal angle between any such pair is at least $ {\pi \over 2} - \frac{C_1}{N} - C_2Nh - \frac{C_3}{\sqrt{N}}, $ for some constants $C_1,C_2,C_3$ independent of $N$ and $h$. This near-orthogonality enables the spectral analysis of such $U_N$ to be reduced to the analysis of each individual cluster. As a consequence, we derive sharp scaling for all singular values of $U_N$, revealing how the geometry of clustered points controls the conditioning of the high-dimensional super-resolution problems. Then we establish min-max error bounds for the recovery of clustered point sources, requiring only an upper bound on the largest cluster size and no knowledge of the geometry within the clusters. These bounds coincide with the optimal rates known in the one-dimensional setting. Furthermore, when the clustered points are in generic position (i.e. do not lie on a low-dimensional algebraic variety) our results indicate that super-resolution in high dimensions is more stable than in one dimension.

papers.title: A counterexample to Kenig's conjecture for the Laplace double-layer operator
papers.abstract: We disprove Kenig's 1994 spectral-radius conjecture for the double-layer operator in every dimension $d\ge2$. For every $t>1/2$ sufficiently close to $1/2$, we construct a bounded simply connected Lipschitz domain with connected boundary such that the double-layer operator on $L^2$ with respect to the surface measure has $\pm \mathrm{i} t$ in its Fredholm essential spectrum. In particular, the essential spectral radius is greater than $1/2$. In the plane, the boundary may be chosen differentiable everywhere and smooth away from a single point. Our planar construction develops a refinement mechanism that produces unbounded growth of adjoint resolvent solutions with fixed forcing while keeping the graph slopes uniformly bounded. A closed recursion for the density and its image under an auxiliary singular integral reduces the growth estimate to a certified inequality for Hermitian $2\times2$ matrices. The certificate uses continuous estimates, exact rational arithmetic and rigorous interval enclosures. Localisation and rescaled graph insertions then produce a weakly null sequence of normalised approximate eigenvectors for the adjoint double-layer operator on one bounded boundary. A compact intertwining relation on Cartesian products of the planar domain with cubes gives the higher-dimensional examples without changing the spectral parameter.

papers.title: The fractional Calder\'on problem on finite Cayley graphs
papers.abstract: We study a Calder\'on-type inverse problem for the spectral fractional Laplacian on finite Cayley graphs. For a known self-adjoint operator, recovery from a single measurement reduces to two requirements: full rank of the boundary (exterior)-to-interior coupling and nonvanishing of the interior solution. We verify both requirements on Cartesian products of arbitrary finite groups with even cycles, using consecutive cyclic halves as the accessible and inaccessible sets. Fractionalization increases the coupling rank, and one fixed nonnegative nonzero input determines every nonnegative potential. Our argument relies on a discrete maximum principle and an explicit resolvent formula.

papers.title: An optimal inequality between nonlinear eigenvalues in convex sets
papers.abstract: Let $\lambda_p(\Omega)$ be the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of the $p$-Laplacian in a bounded convex open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^N$, $N\ge2$. We prove that $p\mapsto\lambda_p(\Omega)^{1/p}/\pi_p$ is strictly decreasing, where $\pi_p^p$ is the first eigenvalue on the unit interval. Consequently, for $1<q<p<\infty$, the sharp upper bound for $\lambda_p(\Omega)^{1/p}/\lambda_q(\Omega)^{1/q}$ is $\pi_p/\pi_q$. This bound is not attained and is approached by slabs, resolving the conjecture on the supremum formulated in the plane by Parini (J. Convex Anal. 2017). The proof combines log-concavity of the first eigenfunction with a vector field constructed from the one-dimensional eigenfunctions. The endpoint limits recover the Hersch--Protter and reverse Cheeger (or Buser) inequalities.

papers.title: Entropic metastability for drifted reflected Brownian motion: quasi-stationary distributions, regularity, and the exit position distribution
papers.abstract: Motivated by entropic metastability and the narrow escape problem, we investigate quasi-stationary distributions for reflected, drifted elliptic diffusions under mixed absorbing-reflecting boundary conditions on a bounded domain. We address two problems, which are solved completely independently of each other. First, using purely probabilistic tools, we prove the existence and uniqueness of a quasi-stationary distribution under minimal regularity assumptions on the coefficients (the case of an unbounded domain is also analyzed). Second, using spectral theory and the theory of strongly continuous semigroups on L p spaces, we study the analytical properties of the quasistationary distribution. We relate it to the principal eigenfunction of the adjoint of the associated (non-symmetric) infinitesimal generator with mixed absorbing-reflecting boundary conditions, and we establish its regularity up to the interface between the two boundary parts. We also fully characterize the law of the exit point when the process is initially distributed according to its quasistationary distribution. In particular, we work on domains in which the absorbing (Dirichlet) and reflecting (Neumann) parts of the boundary meet tangentially, without forming any non-trivial angle, a configuration that raises genuine regularity difficulties for the solutions of the associated mixed boundary value problem.

papers.title: Semiclassical measures for quantized elliptic and parabolic symplectic linear maps of the multidimensional torus
papers.abstract: We study the semiclassical measures associated to the quantum map on the torus obtained by quantizing integer symplectic linear maps, focusing on periodic matrices and certain parabolic matrices. More precisely, we consider the time-one map of the completely integrable flows generated by Hamiltonians of the form H(x, $\xi$) = Q($\xi$)/2 where Q is an integral quadratic form. We prove that the set of semiclassical measures associated to a periodic matrix A coincides with the set of invariant probability measures of A. The semiclassical measures of parabolic matrices on T${}^2$ are explicitly characterized by proving that they have at most three nonzero Fourier coefficients in position. A partial quantum ergodicity statement for parabolic matrices is obtained by proving a sharp bound on the quantum variance and some examples are built in higher dimensions. In particular, starting from T___ there always exist semiclassical measures whose projection on the position has only nonzero Fourier coefficients. Moreover, if Q is isotropic over the rationals, then there exist semiclassical measures whose projection on the position concentrate on some subtori. A link is made with the semiclassical measures of the Laplacian on the torus.

papers.title: Pseudodifferential structure, rigidity, and sharpness for the Steklov problem on differential forms
papers.abstract: We resolve four questions concerning Karpukhin's Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator on differential forms. First, for $0\leq p\leq n-2$, we prove that the operator is classical pseudodifferential of order one and compute its principal symbol, which is elliptic on the coclosed symbol space. This answers Open Question 7.19 in the survey of Colbois, Girouard, Gordon, and Sher [7]. Second, the symbol calculation yields a Weyl law with remainder $O(\tau^{n-2})$, resolving the smooth case of their Open Question 7.23 in [7]. Third, in the critical dimension $n=2p+2$, we show that conformal deformations of the Euclidean ball fixing the boundary metric preserve the full operator. Nonisometric metrics therefore retain all equalities in Karpukhin's initial equality range, disproving the isometry-rigidity assertion of Conjecture 2.12 in [19](the rigidity assertion of Conjecture 7.27 in [7]). Fourth, we establish the all-index sharpness asserted in Conjecture 2.13 in [19](the sharpness assertion of Conjecture 7.27 in [7]) in the class of smooth compact connected oriented Riemannian manifolds with boundary. For $p\geq1$, a shrinking-core construction inspired by the collapsing models of Ann\'e and Takahashi produces manifolds with fixed spherical boundary and explicit two-sided bounds for an initial eigenvalue cluster.

papers.title: Equivalence of local weak and Benjamini--Schramm formulations of Berry's random wave model
papers.abstract: Berry's random wave model predicts that high-energy eigenfunctions of classically chaotic systems can be modeled locally, at the wavelength scale, by the Gaussian monochromatic random wave. Several rigorous formulations of this prediction have been proposed. We prove the equivalence of two such formulations on a closed manifold: local weak limits and Benjamini--Schramm convergence of manifolds decorated by eigenfunctions. The latter considers pointed manifolds equipped with a smooth function, up to isometry, without recording local orthonormal coordinates. The key step is to recover the unaveraged local function law from its orthogonal average using translation invariance and the ergodicity of the random wave. Finally, either formulation implies strong inverse localization, allowing high-energy eigenfunctions to approximate arbitrary solutions of the Euclidean Helmholtz equation, with applications to their nodal sets.

papers.title: Spectrum of the wave equation with Dirac damping on a compact star graph
papers.abstract: We consider the wave equation with a distributional Dirac damping and Dirichlet boundary conditions on a compact interval. It is shown that the spectrum of the corresponding wave operator is fully determined by zeroes of an entire function. Consequently, a considerable change of spectral properties is shown for certain critical values of the damping parameter. We also derive a definitive criterion for the Riesz basis property of the root vectors for an arbitrary placement of a complex-valued Dirac damping. Finally, we consider a generalisation of the problem for compact star graphs and provide insight into the essence of the critical damping constant.

papers.title: Minimal immersions by first eigenfunctions of Riemann surfaces with large conformal automorphism groups. The Klein quartic
papers.abstract: Minimal immersions of closed surfaces into spheres by first eigenfunctions play an important role in both the theory of minimal surfaces and spectral geometry. In this paper, we establish the existence of equivariant conformal minimal immersions of this type for Hurwitz surfaces and other families of %Riemann surfaces with large automorphism group. Finally, we explicitly construct a conformal minimal equivariant immersion of the Klein quartic into the unit sphere $S^{7}$ by first eigenfunctions. Ths immersion is a natural candidate for maximizing the normalized $\lambda_1$ among closed genus-3 surfaces.

papers.title: Upper Bound on the Correlation Energy of a Dense Fermi Gas in the Thermodynamic Limit
papers.abstract: We prove that the random phase approximation provides an upper bound on the correlation energy of a three-dimensional, weakly interacting, Fermi gas in the thermodynamic limit at high density. More precisely, we consider a mean-field scaling regime where the kinetic and interaction Hamiltonian are scaled by $\rho^{-2/3}$ and $\rho^{-1}$, respectively. We use a correlated trial state constructed through a quasi-bosonic Bogoliubov transformation of collective particle--hole excitations associated to patches on the Fermi surface. Key of the proof is to control the position-space localization of the collective excitations. Combined with an iterated Duhamel expansion of the expectation values of (localized) particle number operators we obtain extensive estimates, which justify the reduction to an effective quadratic Hamiltonian and its approximate diagonalization.

papers.title: Optimal eigenvalues on a metric graph with densities
papers.abstract: We introduce and study Laplacians on a finite metric graph endowed with generalized densities, that is, measures of finite mass. One important motivation is that this setting provides a common framework for several interesting classes of operators: discrete graph Laplacians, Kirchhoff Laplacians and Dirichlet-to-Neumann operators on graphs. Our main interest lies in spectral optimization with respect to the underlying measure. In contrast to the setting of domains and manifolds, we prove that a minimal $k$-th eigenvalue exists, whereas the corresponding maximization problem has no meaning. We then establish connections between these optimal eigenvalues and the geometry of the metric graph, including a transparent geometric characterization of the first optimal eigenvalue via the resistance metric, and a Weyl law for the higher optimal eigenvalues.

papers.title: Singularities of Multidimensional Item Response Models and the Rank of the Fisher Information Matrix
papers.abstract: Statistical models in item response theory are known to be singular. This singularity manifests itself as a loss of rank in the Fisher information matrix, and the usual theories underlying AIC and BIC, which assume regularity, cannot be applied without further justification. Chen and colleagues analyzed this degeneracy and nonregular likelihood ratio tests, but their analysis does not identify all the directions that produce degeneracy or their dimensions. In this study, we analyze the entire kernel of the Fisher information matrix as a linear space for multidimensional item response models, separating the degeneracy due to rotations from that due to an over-specified latent dimension without double counting. We determine the dimension of each component and the exact rank of the information matrix, and prove a formula for computing, from the item parameters, the dimension of the degeneracy that remains after these components are removed. These results go beyond establishing the existence of singularity to identifying its causes and extent, providing a foundation for inference and model comparison in IRT.

papers.title: Efimov effect in an internal spectral gap of a three-particle lattice Hamiltonian
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of an Efimov sequence in an internal gap of the essential spectrum of a three-particle lattice Hamiltonian. The system consists of two identical spinless fermions and one distinguishable particle on \(\Z^3\), with repulsive pair interactions. For each fixed fermion-to-third-particle mass ratio \(\gamma>\gamma_*\approx13.6069657\) and total quasi-momentum near \(\pi\mathbf1\), the mixed zero-range coupling is tuned to a simultaneous upper-threshold resonance. Sufficiently strong nearest-neighbour repulsion between the fermions separates the upper fermion-pair two-cluster spectrum from the free three-particle band. Infinitely many discrete eigenvalues accumulate at the lower endpoint of the resulting gap, which coincides with the free upper edge. We establish logarithmic eigenvalue-counting asymptotics with the same positive coefficient as at zero fermion--fermion coupling. This coefficient also governs accumulation above the essential spectrum throughout the closed weak-coupling interval, including its critical endpoint. We classify the channel spectrum near the free upper edge for all nonnegative fermion couplings.

papers.title: A P\"oschl--Teller approximation to the wave equation outside a torus
papers.abstract: We prove dispersive estimates for an approximation to the wave equation in the exterior of a torus. Because no separation of variables into a basis of eigenfunctions and eigenvalues exists in toroidal coordinates for the time harmonic problem, we introduce a related approximate operator for the Dirichlet Laplacian in the exterior of a torus. The approximate operator separates into Schr\"odinger operators with P\"oschl-Teller potentials after freezing $N=N_0$ in the conjugated Laplacian. The operator here which we develop is related to the so-called Mehler-Fock kernel. Using the known solution to the eigenvector and eigenvalue problem of P\"oschl-Teller, a high-frequency analysis of the approximate operator for the wave equation can be made accurately. The operator for this problem gives an angularly truncated $L^1\rightarrow L^{\infty}$ dispersive estimate on compact coordinate collars. Duhamel's principle controls its error for the corresponding exterior wave operator with Dirichlet Laplacian.

papers.title: Zonal states and improved $L^\infty$ bounds for eigenfunctions of magnetic Laplacians on hyperbolic surfaces
papers.abstract: We establish polynomially improved $L^\infty$ bounds for eigenfunctions of magnetic Laplacians on hyperbolic surfaces in the critical energy regime. We also show that, below the critical energy, the H\"ormander bound is saturated by explicit eigenstates, which we call magnetic zonal states. These states resemble zonal harmonics on the sphere and equidistribute on Lagrangian tori in phase space.

papers.title: Combinatorial Courant-Fischer-Weyl Minimax Principle on Cheeger $k$-constants of Weighted Forests
papers.abstract: We present several max-min and minimax characterizations of Cheeger $k$-constants in weighted forests, thereby providing the first combinatorial analogue of the Courant-\\Fischer-Weyl minimax principle. As for applications, we prove that the forest 1-Laplacian variational eigenvalues are independent of the choice of typical indexes; we propose a refined higher order Cheeger inequality which establishes a relationship between Miclo's multiway Cheeger constants and the variational eigenvalues of graph $p$-Laplacians; and we show a purely combinatorial proof for the equality $h_k=\lambda_k(\Delta_1)$ on trees which connects the 1-Laplacian variational eigenvalues and the multiway Cheeger constants.

papers.title: Isodiametric-type upper bounds for Steklov eigenvalues
papers.abstract: Let $n\geq 2$. We establish isodiametric-type upper bounds for Steklov eigenvalues of bounded Lipschitz domains $\Omega$ in Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ and hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^n$. In Euclidean space, we prove \[ D(\Omega)\sigma_k(\Omega)\leq C(n)k, \] with optimal dependence on $k$. For domains in either $\mathbb{R}^n$ or $\mathbb{H}^n$, we establish \[ D(\Omega)\sigma_k(\Omega)\leq C(n)k^2\left(\frac{|\Omega|^{\frac{1}{n}}}{D(\Omega)}\right)^{\frac{n}{n-1}}. \] The exponent of the volume-diameter ratio is optimal in both settings, and with this exponent fixed, the quadratic dependence on $k$ is also optimal. Interpolating the preceding volume-diameter estimate with a volume-normalized Steklov bound, we further obtain \[ D(\Omega)\sigma_k(\Omega)\leq C(n)k^{1+\frac{1}{2n-1}} \] in hyperbolic space. These results answer Open Question 4.37 affirmatively and resolve the hyperbolic part of Open Question 4.35, both posed in [5].

papers.title: Spectra of Random Polynomial Matrices: the Petaloid Law
papers.abstract: We study the distribution of the zeros of $\det P_N(z)$ where $P_N(z)$ is a random monic polynomial matrix, i.e., $P_N(z)=z^dI-\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}A_{j,N}z^j$ for possibly coupled random matrices $A_{j,N}$, scaled to have entrywise variance $O(1/N)$. We provide general conditions under which this distribution almost-surely weakly converges as $N\to\infty$ to a deterministic measure, depending on just the variance and covariance of the entries of the $A_j$. This generalizes the circular, elliptic, and semicircle laws, which concern the special case of this question where $d=1$. Unlike those classical laws, these measures can combine nonuniform two-dimensional densities with singular components supported on curves, producing a variety of petal-shaped regions, inspiring our name ``the petaloid law''. We give explicit formulas for the limiting densities and supports. Under a Gaussianity assumption, we also show that there are almost surely no eigenvalues outside small neighborhoods of the limiting support.

papers.title: Quantitative P\'olya inequalities for annular sectors
papers.abstract: We prove explicit positive corrections to the Dirichlet and Neumann P\'olya inequalities at every positive eigenvalue index of every annular sector. The coefficients depend only on the radii and are uniform in the aperture. Real-order angular integration preserves the exact area term, while directional rounding estimates and radial trials control all frequencies. Optimized bounds attain the sharp circular-arc coefficient for the continuous count. We identify the full sector perimeter asymptotic and a low-index obstruction to using its coefficient throughout the spectrum. The strict Neumann inequality also passes to products with bounded Lipschitz domains.
